followUpQuestions: How does Utrecht compare to other Randstad cities?
What role does student housing play in Utrecht's market?
Which neighborhoods within Utrecht have seen the most growth?
How did COVID-19 affect price trajectories?

answer.intro: House prices in Utrecht have risen by <bold>131% since 2015</bold> — the sharpest relative increase of any major Dutch city, outpacing Amsterdam's 96% and Rotterdam's 108%.<cite>[1]</cite> Several structural forces converge to explain this trend.
answer.supplyBody: Utrecht's historic inner city fundamentally limits outward expansion. Building permits issued in Utrecht fell 23% between 2018 and 2023, while population density continued rising. Strong institutional demand from Utrecht University's 36,000 students further compresses available housing stock.
answer.accessBody: Utrecht Centraal connects Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Den Haag and Eindhoven within 30–45 minutes, positioning it as the functional hub of the Randstad. Commuters displaced by Amsterdam's even higher prices increasingly chose Utrecht as a primary base — a pattern CBS data confirms as a net inflow since 2018.
answer.incomeBody: Average disposable household income in Utrecht Province exceeded the Amsterdam metropolitan area for the first time in 2021. This shifted Utrecht from an "affordable alternative" to a primary high-demand market with its own purchasing power dynamics.
